channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Nazarali Aripov appointed Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to Tajikistan
item.description: Nazarali Aripov has been appointed as the new Ambassador of Kyrgyzstan to Tajikistan by presidential decree. He replaces Erlan Abdyldaev, who served since April 2022 and was later appointed Ambassador to Hungary. Aripov previously served as Consul General in Almaty.

item.title: Kazakhstan Schools Brace for Over 380,000 First-Graders Amidst Teacher Strain
item.description: Kazakhstan anticipates over 380,000 first-graders this academic year, raising concerns about school readiness and teacher workload. Educators note that overcrowded classrooms, with over 20 students, hinder individualized attention and teaching quality, advocating for smaller class sizes of 12-15 students for better learning outcomes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank Maintains Key Rate at 12% Amid Inflationary Pressures
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank has kept its key interest rate at 12% to combat inflation, which stands at 7.3% year-to-date (11.7% annually). Rising fuel and import costs, influenced by geopolitical conflicts, contribute to price increases. The bank aims to curb secondary inflation effects through tight monetary policy.

item.title: US Aims to Isolate Egypt's Second Largest Bank from Global Financial System
item.description: The Trump administration announced new measures to increase financial pressure on Iran and its allies. Following the sanctions, Banque Misr's UAE branch will be unable to conduct US dollar transactions. This action targets Egypt's second-largest bank, aiming to isolate it from the global financial system.

item.title: Bishkek in Global Spotlight: International Media Covers SCO Summit and Nomad Games
item.description: Bishkek is increasingly featured in international media ahead of the SCO summit and World Nomad Games. Outlets like AFP analyze the SCO as a counterbalance to Western influence, highlighting geopolitical dynamics between China, Russia, and other members. Kyrgyzstan's effort to host a major diplomatic and sporting event is also noted.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister arrives in Uzbekistan for state visit
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan for a state visit at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. He was welcomed at Tashkent-Humo International Airport by the Uzbek President. State flags and an honor guard were present for the occasion.

item.title: Chinese magazine features Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary
item.description: A special issue of China's 'Luokai' magazine highlights Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary, detailing reforms and achievements in politics, economy, and culture. It covers bilateral cooperation, investment potential, the Islamic Civilization Center, and the 'Uzbekistan-2030' strategy.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India's Strategic Partnership Shows Growing Momentum
item.description: Uzbek-Indian relations have gained new momentum since 2017, evolving beyond political dialogue to multifaceted practical cooperation. This strategic partnership spans politics, economy, industry, health, digital sectors, education, security, and transport, driven by political will and complementary economies.

item.title: Russia's Foreign Ministry Calls Armenia's Mobilization Statements a Provocation
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova labeled statements by Armenian Security Council Secretary Alen Simonyan regarding accepting Russians in case of mobilization as a provocation. Zakharova stated Simonyan's remarks encourage illegal actions and politicize Armenian hospitality. The ministry expressed regret over Yerevan's public statements undermining bilateral cooperation with Moscow.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presents Parliamentary Diplomacy Experience at Phnom Penh Conference
item.description: Uzbekistan shared its parliamentary diplomacy experience at the II Inter-Parliamentary Conference in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The delegation highlighted the strengthening atmosphere of good neighborliness and cooperation in Central Asia, emphasizing constructive dialogue for conflict resolution.

item.title: Indian PM Modi Pays Respects at Independence Monument in Uzbekistan
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accompanied by Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, laid flowers at the foot of the Independence Monument. He received a brief introduction to the monument's significance and unique features.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi Arrives in Uzbekistan for State Visit
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan on Saturday for a state visit, where he was welcomed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the Tashkent airport. Key events are scheduled for Sunday, including discussions on trade, investment, defense, energy, and education. Agreements are expected to be signed.

item.title: Uzbekistan's startups to gain new opportunities for international market entry
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Digital Technologies met with 500 Global's managing partner to discuss developing the startup ecosystem, increasing venture investments, and facilitating international market access for local startups. The company expressed interest in programs to prepare Uzbek startups for global investment markets and expand their interaction with foreign investors.

item.title: New AIDS center opens in Namangan, enhancing medical care quality
item.description: A new building for the AIDS Center has been commissioned in Namangan region, Uzbekistan. Equipped with modern diagnostic laboratories and patient care facilities, it aims to expand HIV testing, improve patient care, and ensure timely medication. The project, costing over $1.25 million, significantly increases the lab's capacity to 10,000 tests daily.

item.title: Taliban dismisses SCO concerns over Afghan territory threats
item.description: The Taliban has dismissed concerns raised by the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) regarding potential threats emanating from Afghan territory. This statement comes amidst ongoing regional security discussions and Afghanistan's role within the SCO framework. The group's stance aims to reassure neighboring countries about its commitment to preventing cross-border militancy.

item.title: Nearly 400 Trucks Congested at Kazakhstan-Kyrgyzstan Border Crossing
item.description: Approximately 400 trucks are backed up at the Karasu border crossing in Kazakhstan's Zhambyl region, heading towards Kyrgyzstan. The congestion is attributed to a seasonal increase in freight transport and temperature restrictions on truck movement in Kyrgyzstan. Border services are working to manage the flow.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi Arrives in Uzbekistan for State Visit
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has arrived in Uzbekistan for a state visit. He was welcomed at the Tashkent-Humo International Airport by the head of the Uzbek state.

item.title: China plans to deepen cooperation with Kyrgyzstan in multiple sectors
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping outlined plans to expand cooperation with Kyrgyzstan in trade, investment, infrastructure, green minerals, digital economy, clean energy, and AI. He expressed anticipation for jointly developing a new plan for China-Kyrgyzstan relations and noted the countries' evolution to a comprehensive strategic partnership.

item.title: China Aims to Expand Cooperation with Kyrgyzstan in Key Sectors, Says Xi Jinping
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed China's intention to expand cooperation with Kyrgyzstan in trade, investment, infrastructure, green minerals, digital economy, clean energy, and artificial intelligence. He highlighted the strategic partnership and the 'community with a shared future' between the two nations.

item.title: Danish policy of forced contraception in Greenland violated women's rights
item.description: Two independent studies concluded that Denmark's forced contraception policy in Greenland violated women's rights, though experts differed on the scale and systematic nature of the violations. The investigations found that contraception was applied without valid consent, violating women's rights to privacy and family life, and in some cases was degrading.

item.title: China and Kyrgyzstan should always be each other's support, says Xi Jinping
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated that China and Kyrgyzstan should be pillars of each other's development. He emphasized strengthening good-neighborliness, maintaining high-level contacts, and aligning development strategies. Xi also expressed China's willingness to assist Kyrgyzstan's economic development and improve its people's well-being.

item.title: Stone Artifacts Found at Arkutsoy Site May Date Back 320-280 Thousand Years
item.description: Stone tools potentially dating back 320-280 thousand years have been discovered at the Arkutsoy Paleolithic site in Uzbekistan's Tashkent region. If confirmed by lab analysis, Arkutsoy could be recognized as the oldest known archaeological site in Uzbekistan, according to the Academy of Sciences.

item.title: Uzbekistan Raises Cash Payment Limit for Goods Exceeding 400 Base Calculation Amounts
item.description: In Uzbekistan, cash payments are no longer permitted for goods exceeding 400 times the base calculation amount. The limit for non-cash transactions has been increased, previously set at 25 million UZS.

item.title: China and Kyrgyzstan Should Be Pillars of Support for Each Other, Says Xi Jinping
item.description: In an article ahead of his state visit, Chinese President Xi Jinping stated that China and Kyrgyzstan should be pillars of development support for each other. He emphasized strengthening good-neighborliness, maintaining high-level contacts, and deepening cooperation in governance, culture, tourism, and media.

item.title: China and Kyrgyzstan should always be each other's support, says Xi Jinping
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated that China and Kyrgyzstan should be pillars of each other's development. He emphasized strengthening good-neighborliness, maintaining high-level contacts, and aligning development strategies. Xi also expressed China's willingness to assist Kyrgyzstan's economic development and improve its people's well-being.

item.title: Xi Jinping plans new development strategy for China-Kyrgyzstan relations
item.description: Ahead of his state visit, Chinese President Xi Jinping published an article outlining a vision for bilateral relations, emphasizing economic cooperation. He noted China's role as Kyrgyzstan's largest trade partner and investor, highlighting joint projects like the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway and improved transport links.

item.title: SCO's 25th anniversary marked by focus on green cooperation and sustainable development
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) celebrates its 25th anniversary with a strong emphasis on green cooperation and sustainable development. China, as a founding member, actively shares its expertise in ecological civilization and renewable energy, supporting member states in their green transition. The organization promotes renewable energy sources amid global energy shifts.

item.title: US Assumes Control of Venezuelan Oil Reserves, Covering 17 Strategic Fields
item.description: The United States has announced its assumption of control over Venezuela's oil reserves, encompassing 17 strategic fields. These reserves hold confirmed deposits exceeding 65 billion barrels, with expectations of nearly $100 billion in private investment.

item.title: Sadyr Japarov inspects Manas Airport post-reconstruction ahead of international events
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov conducted an unannounced inspection of Manas International Airport following its reconstruction. He assessed the airport's readiness to host high-ranking guests for the upcoming SCO summit and World Nomad Games, emphasizing the need for thorough preparation to enhance Kyrgyzstan's international standing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan-China trade turnover reached $2.6 billion in six months
item.description: The trade turnover between Kyrgyzstan and China amounted to $2.6 billion in the first half of the year, according to Urmat Takirov, head of Kyrgyz Export. Kyrgyz exports to China accounted for $94.2 million of this sum. Exports of Kyrgyz products to China grew by approximately 50 percent compared to the same period last year.

item.title: US delegation to attend Kyrgyzstan's Independence Day celebrations
item.description: A U.S. delegation led by Special Envoy to South and Central Asia Sergio Gor will attend Kyrgyzstan's 35th Independence Day ceremony. The delegation includes Senator Steve Daines and other officials. Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to the U.S. Edil Baisalov views this as a sign of strengthening bilateral relations and growing mutual interest.

item.title: Tajik Government Revises Economic Development Forecast for Next Three Years
item.description: The Tajik government has revised its economic development forecast for the upcoming three years. The updated document indicates a more cautious approach by authorities in assessing certain sectors, including aluminum production and some agricultural products.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces "Presumption of Legitimacy" for Entrepreneurs
item.description: Uzbekistan is introducing a "presumption of legitimacy" for entrepreneurs, meaning all legislative contradictions will be interpreted in their favor. Additionally, 50% of state services for businesses will operate under the "silence is consent" principle.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Launch 75 New Agricultural Enterprises by End of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Agriculture plans to commission 75 new processing and production facilities by the end of 2026, a nearly 19% increase from 2025. These enterprises will focus on food processing, storage, and logistics, aiming to deepen product processing and create jobs.

item.title: President Sadyr Japarov Inspects Manas Airport Following Reconstruction
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov conducted an unscheduled inspection of Manas International Airport after its extensive reconstruction. He reviewed the facilities and grounds, ensuring readiness for upcoming international events like the SCO summit and World Nomad Games. The president stressed the need for high standards in order and security.

item.title: CSTO to Send Military Equipment to Dushanbe to Strengthen Tajik-Afghan Border
item.description: The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) plans to deliver military equipment and necessary weapons to Dushanbe this autumn. The deployment aims to strengthen Tajikistan's border with Afghanistan.

item.title: US Lacks Strategy to End Conflict with Iran, Says Senate Democrat Leader Schumer
item.description: Senate Democrat leader Chuck Schumer stated that the US lacks a strategy to end the conflict with Iran, even six months after hostilities began. Washington reportedly does not know how to exit the current confrontation.

item.title: Uzbekistan collected over 3 trillion soms for IMEI codes in seven years
item.description: Uzbekistan has collected over 3 trillion soms for mobile device IMEI code registration in the past seven years. The UzIMEI system operator stated these payments are not taxes but service fees. The system aims to encourage official imports and the opening of authorized stores.

item.title: Kazakhstan establishes new state body directly accountable to the president
item.description: Kazakhstan has established a new state body, the Security Council Apparatus, which is directly subordinate to and accountable to the President. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed a decree on August 29 to further improve the state management system.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Future Labor Market Prospects Analyzed in Europe, Asia, and Gulf States
item.description: An analysis indicates promising future labor market opportunities for Uzbekistan in Europe, Asia, and Gulf states. Saudi Arabia may require 1.5-2 million additional workers, while the UAE could need 1 million.
